title: TabICL (Tabular In-Context Learning) GitHub repository
why_relevant: Competition’s required reference notebook uses TabICL; understanding install/runtime knobs and data expectations helps reproduce and safely toggle it in kernel.py.
extracted_technique: Use TabICLClassifier with quantile normalization, AMP, and GPU device; fit/predict_proba per CV fold and ensemble across folds.
takeaway: TabICL provides a classifier API suitable for CV-based AUC optimization; treat auto-downloaded checkpoints as external assets and keep a rules-gated fallback to boosting models.

title: TabPFN GitHub repository (PriorLabs)
why_relevant: TabPFN is a strong small-tabular baseline often used for high accuracy; useful as an ensemble member alongside GPU boosting.
extracted_technique: Train-free/low-tuning tabular classifier; generate per-fold OOF and test probabilities and blend with boosting for robustness.
takeaway: TabPFN can deliver strong accuracy on small datasets with minimal tuning; dependency/runtime variability suggests keeping it optional with a clean CatBoost/XGBoost fallback.

title: CatBoost documentation: Training on GPU
why_relevant: GPU CatBoost is a high-accuracy, rules-safe tabular workhorse; GPU support enables repeated CV and longer schedules.
extracted_technique: Use CatBoostClassifier with task_type='GPU', early stopping, and careful regularization; produce predict_proba for ROC-AUC and blend across folds/seeds.
takeaway: CatBoost GPU training is straightforward and fast enough for multi-seed CV; it’s a strong default when pretrained foundation models are disallowed or unstable.

title: XGBoost documentation: GPU support
why_relevant: XGBoost GPU hist is a strong complementary model to CatBoost; blending often improves AUC stability on small tabular datasets.
extracted_technique: Use tree_method='gpu_hist' with early stopping on fold validation; predict probabilities for AUC and ensemble across folds/seeds.
takeaway: GPU-accelerated XGBoost enables broader hyperparameter sweeps and ensembles; pair with strict fold-based validation to avoid overfitting and leakage.
